answer: Willow delay chain: each fake identity costs 5 hours of strictly sequential squaring every epoch. The chain is seeded by the epoch's horizon beacon, so it can't be precomputed; at close a randomly drawn juniper auditor recomputes a sampled segment and rejects any proof whose output or checkpoint hashes mismatch. Squarings can't be split across GPUs or bought in bulk, so 1,000 fakes need 1,000 cores busy 5 h each, every epoch. Limit: faster ASICs shave time, so the delay is set against the fastest known hardware.
